prompts.A:
Create one final-quality raster website SECTION MOCKUP for ADELVA, a Japanese hospitality management implementation partner. This is a proposed desktop webpage section viewed in full, not a poster, diagram, contact sheet, device mockup, or mobile layout. Request portrait canvas approximately 1536 by 2048 pixels so the entire long scrolling section is visible.
The attached White Desert screenshot is a COMPOSITION reference only: borrow its cream introduction above a broad dark photographic field, extraordinary negative space, delicate curved journey line, and quiet editorial typography. Replace ALL polar geography, place names, aircraft, statistics, orange side tab, and original text. No Antarctic landmass, map, snow, ocean labels, foreign logos, travel claims, performance numbers, navigation menu, or CTA.
COMMON LAYOUT: top 19% is warm ivory. Small widely spaced 'ADELVA' at top left, centered large refined dark serif title exactly 'From Strategy to Action', below it clearly legible Japanese title exactly '支援の進め方'. Thin divider then the remaining 81% is the photographic composition. Frame the entire section edge to edge, no desktop/browser chrome. Six precise Japanese labels overlay the lower photographic area in generous quiet zones, in order from top to bottom: '01 課題把握', '02 判断', '03 実行・実装', '04 運用', '05 検証', '06 引継ぎ'. These are the only stage labels, each appears once. Use clean Japanese sans-serif and off-white type with enough size to read. Labels do not sit inside cards. A single fine champagne-colored curved line threads from stage 01 toward stage 06, with six small nodes. Depict the scrolling animation at 65% progress: first four nodes and traveled line warm gold; remaining thin line and nodes quiet muted ivory. One restrained bright progress dot near stage 04. No massive neon trails or repeating glowing halos. The line is a graphic website overlay, never a physical illuminated road. Keep photography discernible in shadows, not murky. No additional body copy or invented slogans.
DIRECTION A — GARDEN PATH, photographic realism. Build an atmospheric but exceptionally believable high-angle aerial photograph of an ORIGINAL fictional contemporary Japanese inn's garden and low pavilion. Almost overhead, allowing the eye to travel DOWN the frame. A single gently curving pale stone footpath starts near upper center, bends a little left through moss, low ferns, slate and dark restrained greenery, then curves right toward a low timber-and-plaster hospitality pavilion at the bottom. Small hints of warm interior lighting, coherent architecture, realistic roof details, natural overcast late-afternoon light. Do not copy a recognizable existing hotel. The garden is elegant and restrained, not jungle or an enormous resort. The path and muted terrain establish spacious, low-detail reading zones; do not flood all empty areas with trees. The photographed path stays visible alongside the fine overlay line, creating an intelligible relationship without a garish glow. Put stage labels alternating left and right of the central path with spacious separation. Show visible fine stone, moss and timber textures, natural material colors, deep olive/charcoal and warm gray. Upper part represents entrance, lower part pavilion; no sunrise-to-sunset transformation, no before/after. No people. This must look like a convincing art-directed photography-led finished website section, NOT a simplistic illustrated garden plan.

TOP PHOTO corresponds to labels 01 and 02: a thoughtful hotel owner/manager and operations leader at the same timber table in a quiet hospitality interior, viewed candidly from a slight elevated side angle, attentively examining the same plain paper document, real human proportions, no posed handshake or camera-facing smile, no readable private data or metrics. MIDDLE PHOTO corresponds to 03 and 04: two hospitality professionals verifying a real service workflow at a refined hotel reception desk, one demonstrating and one observing, subtle tablet or unbranded checklist, uncluttered believable reception and hands. One coherent hotel atmosphere, different actions clearly recognizable, age-appropriate adult professionals in understated charcoal/cream work attire. Avoid generic corporate stock-photo grins, crowds, blurry fake hands, invented readable charts, logos, staged key handovers, or luxury vacation guest scenes. The three photographs form the section's imagery, linked by the process line; photorealistic human detail is essential.
